Painted large in one line along the upper fuselage side, above the doorways, the single word "TECHHALLA" in bold white spray-stencil block capitals, worn and chipped, the only lettering on the vehicle. It rides high on four gigantic deep-lug tires and carries stunt-show prop multi-tube rocket launcher pods low on its side. Beside the front tire on the camera side stands the show's hostess, a glamorous woman in her early thirties, tall and athletic, long honey-blonde hair, red bikini, straw cowboy hat and cowboy boots, one hand on the tire, looking toward the ramp. Straight ahead of the truck's nose, mid-floor, a massive steel launch ramp built for monster trucks: its driving deck clearly wider than the whole truck, tires included, low entry lip flat on the dirt facing the truck, rising toward the left on heavy scaffolding. Beyond it, at the far left edge, a big blue and yellow inflatable landing airbag.

Shot type: wide

Source: low late-afternoon sun from the left, behind the airbag side
Quality: hard sun, long shadows, dust glowing in the air

Shadows follow that source.

Natural face texture.
Flyaway hairs under the hat brim. Chipped olive paint, mud spatter, scuffed rubber.
Sky clipped to plain white, wheel wells blocked up and noisy.
A milky veil and a soft streak of flare from the dusty lens.

Candid stance, catalog-unaware.
Plain, slightly warm-shifted color straight out of the phone, an ordinary snapshot.

Real amateur phone footage shot by a spectator from the grandstand at an open-air monster truck show. <<img1>> is the first frame; the video starts exactly on it. Keep its arena, crowd, light, vehicle, hostess, ramp and airbag exactly as shown.

0-5s: [Wide, shaky] Crowd roaring. The spectator in the black cap in the foreground turns to the lens, screaming and pumping his fist. Behind him the hostess climbs the front tire and swings in through the open side doorway.
5-10s: [Digital zoom in] The engine fires with a violent bark and a puff of exhaust, revving hard, the body rocking on its suspension. Both rotors spin up to blurred discs, dust blasts outward, the truck rolls toward the ramp, camera panning left.
10-14s: [Zoom out, long tilt up] Engine screaming at full throttle, it charges up the ramp, launches off the top and keeps climbing steeply on its rotors, far above the top row of the grandstand, until it hangs small against the bright sky, several times the height of the ramp. 14-18s: [Tilt down follow] The hostess steps to the side doorway and jumps feet first, a very long fall, landing on her back in the centre of the airbag, which caves in deeply. She sits up laughing, arms raised.

The man bounces on the airbag, laughing.
23-27s: [Zoomed on the truck in the sky, then whip down] The hovering truck dips its nose toward the empty ramp. The tube pods on its fuselage side flash as rockets shoot out of their tubes one after another, white smoke trails streaking from the helicopter down to the ramp, which erupts in a huge orange fireball. The blast shakes the phone, exposure blows out, the whole grandstand jumps to its feet.
27-30s: [Stepped digital zoom in] Grainy, wobbly punch-in on the cockpit glass: the hostess at the controls in her cowboy hat, grinning and waving. Hold on her.

[AUDIO]
Diegetic only, phone mic clipping. Loudest by far: the raw unmuffled V8 monster truck engine, crackling idle, savage revs, full-throttle scream up the ramp, still bellowing overhead. Under it: rotor thump, crowd roar, rocket whooshes, booming explosion. No background music. No subtitles.

Photorealistic raw phone video, coherent physics, stable characters and vehicle design, legible TECHHALLA lettering, natural motion blur, one unbroken take.

Then animate 2 clips with Seedance 2.5: a 20s one to set the tone and a 30s one for the fight.

Here they are, hope they help!

PROMPT 1⃣ · SETTING THE TONE (20s)
Refs: [Image1] environment · [Image2] nun sheet · [Image3] fallen angel sheet

Dark-fantasy standoff filmed like an epic Hollywood blockbuster, real footage look, anamorphic lens, crushed blacks, saturated magenta flesh walls, sulfur yellow and acid green pools, thick god rays, no dialogue, no fighting, overwhelming tension and awe. Setting: the living-flesh cave of [Image1]. Nun: [Image2], white habit, cracked porcelain kintsugi mask with no mouth, big rusty machete. Fallen angel: [Image3], rusted iron body, burning wings, cracked dry porcelain face with no tears, barbed-wire halo, so colossal that the nun barely reaches its ankle and its wings touch both walls of the cave.
Spatial continuity: one fixed geography for the whole film. The nun enters from the near end of the cave and stops in the center of the sulfur arena. The dark far end of the cave lies straight ahead of her, and that is where the angel rises. The angel is always in front of her, never behind or beside her. Keep screen direction consistent in every shot: the nun on the left side of the frame facing right, the angel on the right side facing left.

Shot 1 (0-2s): Extreme wide abyssal shot from high in the cave ceiling, the tiny white nun walks into the empty arena far below, god rays falling around her.
Shot 2 (2-4s): Slow tracking at ground level beside her boots, sulfur crust cracking under each step, machete hanging from her hand.
Shot 3 (4-6s): Close-up, her porcelain mask turns slowly, scanning the cave. The ground trembles, dust and spores rain from the ceiling, the acid pools ripple.
Shot 4 (6-8s): Over-the-shoulder from behind the nun looking ahead into the darkness at the far end of the cave: deep in the gloom, two burning points ignite high above, far higher than she expected.
Shot 5 (8-11s): Slow push-in toward the far end: out of the penumbra the colossal fallen angel steps forward, its body emerging from the shadows piece by piece, rusted iron catching the god rays, each step shaking the floor and sending ripples across the acid pools.
Shot 6 (11-14s): Extreme low angle from the floor in front of the angel: its giant wings unfold and ignite one after the other in a massive burst of flame that turns the whole cave orange, the god rays turn red, a storm of embers fills the air. The camera tilts up and up along its body to reveal its full impossible height, the barbed-wire halo flaring red-hot.
Shot 7 (14-16s): Reverse shot from high behind the angel's shoulder looking down at the tiny nun far below, she holds her ground in the center of the arena, embers falling around her.
Shot 8 (16-18s): Extreme close-up of the angel's cracked porcelain face lowering toward her, dry and expressionless, firelight flickering in the cracks.
Shot 9 (18-20s): Wide shot in profile, held: the tiny white nun on the left raises her machete, the colossal burning angel on the right towers over her with its wings spread wall to wall, an empty floor of sulfur between them. End on this held image, no fade, no cut to black.

Real footage look, epic scale, heavy atmosphere, no fighting, no blood, no tears, stable characters, consistent spatial continuity and colossal scale throughout.

PROMPT 2⃣ · THE FIGHT (30s)
Refs: [Image1] nun sheet · [Image2] fallen angel sheet · [Image3] still from clip 1

Brutal dark-fantasy battle filmed like an epic Hollywood blockbuster, real footage look, anamorphic lens, crushed blacks, saturated magenta flesh walls, sulfur yellow and acid green pools, burning orange firelight, god rays, speed ramps from full speed into razor-sharp slow motion, rapid-fire hard cuts every 1 second in the action beats, whip pans, crash zooms, constant motion, no pauses. [Image3] is the reference for the cave, the lighting and the positions of both characters; the video does not open on that exact frame. Nun: [Image1], white habit, cracked porcelain kintsugi mask with no mouth, big rusty machete that she grips firmly in her hand in every single shot, she never drops or releases it. Fallen angel: [Image2], rusted iron body, burning wings, cracked dry porcelain face mask with no tears, barbed-wire halo, colossal, many times taller than the nun.
Spatial continuity: one fixed geography as in [Image3]. The nun starts on the left of the arena facing right, the angel stands on the right facing left, the big dark boulder on the far right, the cave opening behind them. Keep screen direction consistent: the nun moves left to right toward the angel, the angel attacks right to left.

Shot 1 (0-2s): Over-the-shoulder from behind the nun, her white veil and machete in the foreground, the colossal angel in the background at the far end of the arena starts charging its attack, wings igniting; the nun breaks into a sprint toward it, the angel sweeps its burning wing down and a towering tidal wave of roaring fire, twenty meters high, races across the floor toward her, swirling with molten embers and black smoke.
Shot 2 (2-3s): She leaps sideways onto the flesh wall and runs along it horizontally, defying gravity, the wave of fire passing below her.
Shot 3 (3-4s): Whip pan, a second burning wing strike smashes the wall where she was, she kicks off and flips across the cave to the opposite wall, landing crouched on it sideways.
Shot 4 (4-5s): Crash zoom, she springs up and thrusts the machete forward without letting go of it: a blinding spell of white holy light bursts from the tip of the blade in a spear of light.
Shot 5 (5-6s): The colossal angel twists aside at the last instant, the spear of light misses by inches and blasts a glowing crater into the flesh wall behind it.
Shot 6 (6-7s): Close-up of the angel's porcelain mask turning toward her, its halo heating white-hot.
Shot 7 (7-8s): The halo fires a blazing vortex of white-hot fire and molten gold that spirals across the cave; she bounces from wall to wall to ceiling like a ricochet, the fire vortex chasing her and scorching the rock behind her.
Shot 8 (8-9s): The angel stamps its giant iron foot, the floor cracks open, acid pools erupt as columns of green liquid.
Shot 9 (9-10s): She leaps between the rising acid columns and falling slabs, each jump longer and higher than humanly possible, gaining speed.
Shot 10 (10-11s): The angel beats both wings: thousands of burning feathers shoot at her like a meteor shower of fiery blades, each leaving a trail of flame.
Shot 11 (11-12s): She spins the machete in a blur, feathers sliced in half exploding into sparks around her.
Shot 12 (12-13s): She runs straight up the cave wall toward the ceiling, the angel's huge hand crushes the rock just below her heels, she pushes off the ceiling and dives down toward it with full momentum.
Shot 13 (13-15s): Wide, the angel rears back and its whole body ignites: a colossal inferno of fire spirals into its chest and halo like a miniature sun, flames erupting from every crack in its iron, the walls glowing red-hot, while the nun dives at it from above.
Shot 14 (15-20s): Frozen time. The nun leaps and rises into the air as if levitating, body arched in attack position, machete raised over her head toward the angel's face. At the peak of the leap time locks completely. Slow 360 orbit around her suspended in mid-air: embers hang as perfect beads of light, burning feathers float motionless like glowing blades, acid droplets hang as glassy green spheres with perfect surface tension, the angel's charged fire frozen as a still sphere of flame in its chest, the angel's face frozen inches from her blade. Only she moves: her head tilts slightly toward the mask. Time snaps back to full speed.
Shot 15 (20-21s): Slow motion impact, her machete strikes the angel's porcelain mask: the mask shatters into hundreds of porcelain shards that spin through the firelight, the charged attack collapses in a burst of sparks.
Shot 16 (21-22s): Reverse shot, the shards rain down around the nun as she lands on the angel's shoulder.
Shot 17 (22-24s): Wide, the colossal angel staggers, its halo dims, it crashes down onto both knees, the impact shakes the whole cave, rocks fall from the ceiling.
Shot 18 (24-26s): Rapid-fire cuts: she yanks the angel's head back by the barbed-wire halo, slams her boot onto its chest, forcing it down, the angel's broken face looks up at her, embers exploding around them.
Shot 19 (26-30s): Final shot: the nun leaps high one last time, spins in the air and comes down with a savage two-handed overhead swing of the rusty machete straight at the angel's neck, full speed, all her weight behind it, a shockwave of dust and embers bursting outward from the force of the swing. Crash zoom on the blade, hard cut exactly at the instant before the blade touches, the last frame is the blade about to hit. No fade, the blow never lands on screen.

Real footage look, epic scale, heavy atmosphere, no blood, no gore, no tears, the nun always holding her machete, stable characters, consistent spatial continuity and colossal scale throughout.

Let me know what you think!

Create an approximately 2:3 vertical, authentic low-light smartphone mirror selfie. A young adult woman is seated or lightly reclining inside a warm private interior, photographing herself through a mirror with a dark carved wooden frame. The image should unmistakably feel like an everyday phone selfie rather than a professionally produced beauty portrait, retaining softness, limited low-light detail, subtle noise and imperfect domestic intimacy.  Position the subject from the left side toward the center of the frame. The phone must stay on frame right at roughly face height, partially obscuring both the face and the background. Preserve the reflected orientation exactly rather than automatically correcting left and right. Her face remains in a natural profile pointing toward frame right. Her gaze rests near the phone screen or her reflected image rather than the camera lens. Her lips are naturally closed or barely parted, and the expression is quiet, relaxed and slightly absent-minded, without a deliberate smile or pout.  Preserve a softly slender face, natural jawline, delicate side-profile nose and gently shaped lips. Use soft natural makeup influenced by romantic East Asian lifestyle and social-media portrait styling: a sheer softly diffused base that still retains genuine skin depth, naturally dark brows, extremely subtle eyeliner or lash-root definition, understated gray-brown or beige-brown eyeshadow, restrained peach or nude-apricot blush, and hydrated rose, dusty pink or nude-pink lips. Avoid aggressive contouring, an exaggerated V-line jaw or oversized eyes.  Her hair is natural black to deep black-brown, long and highly voluminous, with a center or near-center part and long face-framing bangs. Most of the hair falls heavily toward frame left. The lower lengths form loose, imperfect waves rather than polished salon curls. Allow overlapping strands, mild frizz, irregular wave ends and some loss of micro-detail in the darkest areas from smartphone noise reduction.  She wears a warm-white off-shoulder Bardot-style ruched blouse with puffed sleeves. Both shoulders and the collarbone region remain visible, with elasticized gathered sleeve openings resting on the upper arms. The neckline is low and the center of the garment contains naturally gathered, overlapping and compressed white fabric. Preserve the garment's actual coverage rather than artificially altering the body's proportions. The material is lightweight, soft and opaque, turning slightly creamy under warm light. Keep the folds irregular and physically believable instead of smoothing the blouse into a pristine formal gown.  Visible skin includes the face, neck, collarbones, shoulders, upper chest and the portion of chest visible within the neckline, upper arms, forearm, phone-holding hand and fingers, plus part of a bent knee or leg in the lower foreground. The abdomen, back and hips are not clearly shown and should not be invented.  Use a light warm-ivory to pale beige-apricot complexion. The skin should look fine, soft and gently creamy while retaining natural depth and subtle tonal variation. Its visual texture should suggest skin that would feel warm, soft and lightly supple to the touch rather than plastic or poreless.  Translate the mood into physical lighting rather than vague atmospheric light. Use mixed-temperature practical indoor illumination: a warm approximately 3000–3400K lamp or tungsten-like source comes from the front and slightly toward frame right, possibly a little below eye level, creating amber-golden diffuse reflections across the phone-holding hand, forearm, shoulders and upper chest. A weaker cooler source from frame left—such as window light, a pale wall or ambient daylight—gently lifts the shadows. Allow warm orange and more neutral gray-cool regions to coexist across the skin and white fabric. Retain real shadows beside the nose, beneath the hair and around the phone; do not add studio rim lighting.  Add a very delicate silver necklace with a small abstract loop, droplet or curved-metal pendant. Thin silver rings appear on the phone-holding fingers. The nails are moderately long and naturally pink or nude-pink, with believable finger spacing and wrist tension.  The phone is a silver or pale-gray older-generation smartphone with vertically stacked dual rear cameras, inside a clear or pale-gray case. Preserve a rectangular sticker and a slim gray phone-grip accessory on the back. Any sticker lettering should remain mirrored, blurry or unreadable instead of becoming crisp AI-generated forward-facing text.  Allow a bent knee or leg to enter the lower foreground, appearing slightly enlarged because it is closer to the mirror/camera. This foreground obstruction is important to the spontaneous seated-selfie feeling and should not be cleaned out for the sake of perfect composition.  Keep the domestic environment recognizable. Frame right contains large areas of honey-brown or amber-brown wood paneling or cabinet doors. Frame left has a cooler pale-gray or creamy wall. A dark carved wooden mirror frame intrudes naturally along the upper and upper-left edges. Behind the subject hangs a framed decorative artwork containing only soft pink, muted blue and floral-like shapes. The phone, hair and body should obscure parts of the room.  Simulate an older smartphone rear main camera photographing through a mirror, roughly resembling a 26–30mm full-frame-equivalent phone lens, with the mirror distance reducing the harshness of the wide-angle perspective. Keep the subject, phone and nearby room broadly recognizable rather than using professional shallow-focus bokeh. Include mild JPEG compression, low-light noise reduction, slightly smeared dark hair detail, minor color shifts, uneven exposure and fine digital grain. Allow a slight tilt, off-center crop and imperfect framing. Avoid HDR, aggressive sharpening and commercial skin retouching.  The final image should feel like a romantic low-light mirror selfie in a warm wood interior, with soft East Asian social-media portrait styling and subtle 2000s/2010s nostalgia—something that had quietly lived in a phone photo album for years rather than a modern studio image recreated to look nostalgic.  She had just raised the phone in the warm room. The light has already been resting across her shoulders and hand for a while; now she is still looking near the screen, and in the next moment she may lower the phone and return to whatever had been interrupted.  Negative prompt: studio portrait, direct eye contact, front-facing pose, perfect symmetry, plastic skin, heavy makeup, V-shaped face, oversized eyes, HDR, oversharpening, cinematic rim light, teal-orange grading, strong bokeh, clean white studio, missing phone, wrong mirror orientation, readable fake text, extra fingers, deformed hand, perfect hair, overexposed skin, hyper-detailed pores.

2x2 grid, 16:9, pick different stunning subjects: COUNTERFACTUAL   the vessel/station exists. Nothing else is suspended.
INTENT     indifference of the environment; a built thing in a place that will not help it
UNKNOWNS   sun direction ;  albedo of nearby bodies ;  orbit ;  exposure
WHAT THE ABSENCE OF AIR DELETES
  no scattering ⇒ NO aerial perspective. Distant objects are as contrasty and saturated as near ones.
             ⇒ scale and distance become genuinely unreadable — this is a real and reported phenomenon,
               and it should be the FEEL of the shot, not corrected away.
  no scattering ⇒ NO ambient fill. The only fill is BOUNCE: planetshine (and it carries the planet's
             colour — blue-white off ocean/cloud, ochre off Mars, grey off lunar regolith), or light
             kicked off the vessel's own hull. Shadows are near-black, and what little lives in them is
             coloured by whatever bounced it.
  no scattering ⇒ NO visible beams, no godrays, no haze, no volumetric anything. A searchlight in vacuum
             is invisible except where it lands.
  no air     ⇒ NO smoke trails, no contrails, no billowing dust clouds, no fire that spreads as flame.
             Explosive decompression vents a brief directional jet that disperses instantly and does not
             bloom into a fireball.
  no air     ⇒ NO banking, no airfoils doing anything, no swooping turns. Attitude changes come from
             discrete RCS pulses — short, hard, directional, and they must be POINTED correctly for the
             rotation shown (a pitch up fires a specific pair). Main thrust changes velocity, not heading.
  no air     ⇒ a rocket plume EXPANDS as it leaves the bell (no back-pressure to confine it), flaring into
             a wide translucent cone — not a tight blue pencil.
  on an airless surface, kicked dust follows BALLISTIC parabolas and lands. It does not hang, billow,
             swirl, or form a cloud. Apollo footage is the reference.
THE EXPOSURE BUDGET (decisive)
  sunlight at 1 AU is full daylight ⇒ a sunlit hull exposes at roughly sunny-16.
             ⇒ at that exposure STARS DO NOT REGISTER. A correctly exposed sunlit spacecraft sits against
               a BLACK sky. A dense starfield behind a bright hull is two exposures claiming to be one.
             ⇒ the honest version: black sky, or a hull in shadow/planetshine with stars, never both bright.
  the terminator on any sphere is HARD and high-contrast — no soft wrap, no twilight band (unless the body
             has an atmosphere, which then glows as a thin limb arc and must be lit from the same sun)
OVERDETERMINATION   sun direction recovered from hull shading, from every cast shadow, from the planet's
                    own terminator, and from specular glints — one vector, and the planet's phase must
                    agree with the vessel's lighting
HONEST      one sun, one bounce source, one exposure: brutal contrast, black fill, no medium anywhere
FORBIDDEN   visible light beams, haze, or volumetric shafts in vacuum ;
            a brilliantly sunlit hull against a rich starfield ;
            shadow detail with no reflective body present to have filled it ;
            distant ships veiled or desaturated by "distance" where there is no air to veil them ;
            spacecraft banking into turns, or trailing smoke ;
            an explosion that fireballs and billows ;
            dust rising in clouds on an airless body ;
            a soft, gradual day/night terminator on an airless world ;
            RCS thrusters firing in a direction that does not produce the rotation depicted ;
            engine exhaust as a tight collimated beam.

Build the visual system around a bright, low saturation palette. Use pale lavender or soft lilac as the dominant background, deep plum for oversized typography, cool silver gray as a restrained secondary graphic color, and pearl white or light gray for clothing.

The overall look should feel refined, modern, fashion editorial, and visually striking, with realistic skin texture, natural hair strands, believable fabric folds, clean photographic lighting, strong typography, controlled negative space, and full bleed composition.

Create these four layout variations:

Keep the face attractive, recognizable, and mostly aligned. Do not excessively duplicate the eyes, lips, nose, or other facial features. The effect should feel like refined editorial photo editing, not digital distortion. Add oversized horizontal “SHIFT” typography in deep plum.

A father appears to be waiting alone in a fog-filled hospital corridor. Elsewhere, his elderly mother quietly peels an orange for his sleeping little son. A sudden hospital phone call interrupts the family's evening. The boy's mother rushes to the hospital carrying him.
When she arrives, we discover the father has already died. The man we have been watching is his lingering presence, waiting to see his little boy one final time.
And the child has saved him a piece of orange.

EXACT 10-SHOT EDIT
SHOT 01 | 00:00–00:02.0
THE WAITING MAN
REFERENCE 1: EXACT HOSPITAL CORRIDOR WIDE SHOT.
A man sits slumped against the left corridor wall, knees drawn up, exhausted and motionless. A paper coffee cup rests beside him.

85mm close-up. Green fluorescent spill across his exhausted face, a thin red reflection crossing his neck.
His hands are clasped so tightly his knuckles are pale. A distinctive silver wedding ring is visible.

SHOT 03 | 00:03.6–00:05.6
THE ORDINARY EVENING
REFERENCE 2: GRANDMOTHER PEELING ORANGE BESIDE SLEEPING CHILD.
Exact original wide kitchen composition.
An elderly grandmother sits peeling an orange beneath a warm pleated lamp. Her little grandson sleeps with his face against folded arms on the table.
Cold blue light enters through the kitchen doorway. Amber light illuminates her hands. Everything beyond the table sinks into smoky emerald darkness.
She glances affectionately toward him.
For a moment, the world feels completely safe.

Her aged hand gently places a fresh orange segment inside the sleeping boy's small palm.

Over the mother's shoulder.

The father stands up immediately, hopeful, almost relieved.
The young mother walks toward him carrying the little boy.
He moves toward them, ready to embrace his son.

NO VFX. NO GHOST GLOW. NO TRANSPARENCY.

SHOT 10 | 00:17.0–00:20.0

The mother holds her son and faces the hospital room, unaware of the father's presence behind her.
The boy, awake on her shoulder, looks directly into his father's eyes.
The father stands motionless in the cyan fog.
The boy slowly reaches out his tiny open palm.

He whispers with complete innocence:

The father's expression breaks. His eyes fill, but he doesn't sob.
He slowly reaches toward the boy's outstretched hand.
Their fingertips approach, almost touching.
The father gives the smallest, grateful smile.
At exactly 00:19.5, CUT TO BLACK before their hands meet.
A final soft exhale.
Absolute silence at 00:20.0.
NO TEXT. NO TITLE CARD. NO EXPLANATION.
SOUNDTRACK: ORIGINAL 20-SECOND COMPOSITION
Musical architecture: A rapidly evolving, emotionally overwhelming minimal score, built from an approximately 84 BPM heartbeat pulse. Use low bowed cello, trembling high strings, felt piano, dark sub-bass, degraded analog synth and intimately recorded environmental sounds.
The score must remain continuous across all 10 shots while the physical sound source changes.
00:00–00:03.6
Cold electrical ambience. Isolated hospital beep. Deep, barely audible heartbeat. A distant two-note minor piano motif. Very sparse, intense silence around the whispered dialogue.
00:03.6–00:07.0
Hospital beep rhythm transfers into the sound of orange peel tearing. Introduce warm, fragile piano harmonics. The phone vibration suddenly interrupts the gentle rhythm, creating immediate dread.
00:07.0–00:10.5
A low bowed cello enters. Phone vibrations, glass clinks and distant siren become rhythmic elements. Introduce a deep repeating pulse with dissonant string tremolo, accelerating the perceived emotional pace without speeding up the actual tempo.
00:10.5–00:14.3
Elevator motor merges with the pulse. Rising cello harmonics and an ascending two-note felt-piano melody build hope and fear simultaneously. A narrow-band electrical drone grows beneath the mother's breathing. No percussion drums.
00:14.3–00:17.0
At the sight of the father's body, abruptly remove the heartbeat rhythm.
Introduce a restrained, dissonant low string cluster, then near silence.
The emotional shock must land through the sudden absence of rhythm rather than a loud impact.
00:17.0–00:20.0
As the boy reaches out with the orange, resolve the dissonance into a heartbreaking, warm minor-to-major suspended piano and cello harmony.
The boy's whispered line must be completely intelligible.
A faint, intimate cello vibrato continues beneath the father's final expression.
Cut the music instantly at 19.5 seconds.
End with a solitary human breath and absolute silence.
EDITING LANGUAGE
Every cut must connect emotionally or rhythmically.
Hospital beep → orange peel.
Orange peel → phone vibration.
Phone vibration → siren and glass.
Glass clink → hospital monitor.
Hospital monitor → elevator motor.
Elevator clunk → hospital room revelation.
Flatline → boy's voice.
Boy's voice → silence.
Shots 1–2 establish mystery and urgency.
Shots 3–4 establish tenderness and the orange.
Shots 5–6 establish family and a sudden crisis.
Shots 7–8 build suspense as mother and son arrive.
Shot 9 delivers a clear, shocking reversal.
Shot 10 converts the shock into devastating love.
Use controlled match cuts, physically believable camera moves, natural focus changes and consistent character appearances.
PERFORMANCE
No theatrical crying, obvious supernatural gestures or exaggerated facial animation.
Father: Profound exhaustion, urgent anticipation, finally the release of someone who has waited for one thing more important than his own death.
Grandmother: Unhurried, loving, physically delicate. Her simple gesture quietly begins the entire story.
Mother: Barely holding herself together, carrying her son protectively, with practical gestures and silent terror. She never sees the father's spirit.
Boy: Natural sleepy innocence, no fear of his father. He recognizes him immediately. His final gesture should feel instinctive, not staged.
ABSOLUTE VISUAL RESTRICTIONS
Maintain the exact reference-world cinematography and color palette. No blue-white overexposure, no glossy modern lighting, no supernatural smoke bursts, no dissolving ghosts, no VFX morphs, no stylized transitions, no digital glitches, no excessive camera movement, no slow motion, no floating particles, no artificial tears, no captions, no logos.
The two appearances of the father in Shot 09 must be recognizably identical. His physical body lies motionless; his standing spirit is visible only to the boy. No confusing doubles before the reveal.
Preserve the same little boy in grandmother's kitchen and the elevator, with the same clothing and orange segment.
The entire film should look like 10 carefully selected frames from a single beautifully photographed feature film.
EMOTIONAL INTENTION
The final twist is not simply that the father is dead.
It is that the last piece of ordinary love he receives comes from his sleeping little son, passed down through the gentle hands of his own mother.
Three generations. One orange. One unfinished goodbye.
End on the unbearable tenderness of two hands that will never quite touch.

A's voice timbre references Audio 1. Use its vocal identity, not its recorded words.

SETTING AND STYLE
Empty rooftop above Shibuya at dusk. Photorealistic rooftop and distant skyline; hand-drawn 2D anime characters with clean lines and cel shading. Match lighting and contact shadows while preserving anime faces.
A stays screen-left, B screen-right. One sturdy table stands between them toward the foreground. Maintain screen direction.
A holds one katana throughout. One plain round white-frosted cake rests on one wooden cutting board, initially on B's side of the table and visible from the first frame. One fork rests on a ceramic saucer beside B.

Low-angle medium-wide two-shot showing both characters, table and cake.
A plants her feet and raises the katana overhead with a two-handed grip. Bright teal energy coils around the blade. Wind lifts her hair and costume edges; one circular light ripple spreads beneath her feet. Keep her face, hands and sword clearly visible.
B looks from the raised blade to the cake and remains still during the line.
Dialogue, 0.3-1.8 seconds:
A says: "これで、おわりだ！"
Voice timbre reference Audio 1. Lip sync. Speak once in Japanese, confidently and clearly. Finish before 2.0 seconds, then close A's mouth.
Instrumental low strings and percussion build beneath a magical hum. Hard cut.
Shot 2 (4.0-10.0 seconds): THE CAKE CUT
One uninterrupted three-quarter medium shot. Show A's grip and sword, B's hands, the entire cake and tabletop together. Steady camera.
4.0-6.5 seconds: A holds the sword overhead. B pushes the cutting board's edge, sliding board and cake together to the center of the table, directly beneath the blade. The table remains fixed.
6.5-7.2 seconds: B releases the board and withdraws both hands fully to her side. Briefly hold with her hands clearly outside the blade's path.
7.2-8.5 seconds: Only after B's hands are clear, A performs exactly one powerful downward stroke. Feet planted, two-handed grip consistent. A short, brilliant teal arc follows the blade.
Show the blade physically contacting the cake before it separates.
The blade cuts through the cake's center and stops at the board. Exactly two equal semicircular halves remain upright on the board, with a narrow gap and visible fresh sponge cross-sections. The board and table stay intact.
8.5-10.0 seconds: A lifts the blade slightly to reveal the clean cut, then holds still. The teal light fades. B calmly admires the neatly divided cake.
Audio: one sharp sword whoosh, then a soft cake-slicing sound. Stop the dramatic music and magical hum abruptly when the two halves are revealed. No dialogue. Hard cut.
Shot 3 (10.0-12.0 seconds): JUST DESSERT
Medium two-shot, A left and B right. Keep both cake halves visible.
B casually picks up the fork from the saucer. A small ceramic clink. She looks at the cake with her usual calm expression and closed lips.
A looks from the cake to B's fork. Her confidence disappears. Her sword points downward beside her body.
No dialogue. Fork clink and faint rooftop ambience only. Hard cut.
Shot 4 (12.0-15.0 seconds): THE FAMILIAR FACE
Close-up of A, preserving Image 1's facial design.
Eyes widen, pupils become small, eyebrows rise. Lips part slightly once, then remain still. Her familiar stunned, uncomprehending expression.
A short, controlled push-in. Hold her face for the final full second, with only tiny shoulder trembling.
No dialogue or vocal reaction. End directly on A.

AUDIO CONTROL
Exactly one spoken sentence: A's line in Shot 1. After 2.0 seconds, both characters produce zero vocal sound.
Keep the specified instrumental music, sword effects, fork clink and ambient wind.
No improvised speech, narration, inner monologue, gasps, grunts, screams, laughter, vocal breaths, choir or vocal samples. Never replay Audio 1's recorded words.

PROMPT 1⃣ · SETTING THE TONE (20s)
Refs: [Image1] environment · [Image2] nun sheet · [Image3] fallen angel sheet

Dark-fantasy standoff filmed like an epic Hollywood blockbuster, real footage look, anamorphic lens, crushed blacks, saturated magenta flesh walls, sulfur yellow and acid green pools, thick god rays, no dialogue, no fighting, overwhelming tension and awe. Setting: the living-flesh cave of [Image1]. Nun: [Image2], white habit, cracked porcelain kintsugi mask with no mouth, big rusty machete. Fallen angel: [Image3], rusted iron body, burning wings, cracked dry porcelain face with no tears, barbed-wire halo, so colossal that the nun barely reaches its ankle and its wings touch both walls of the cave.
Spatial continuity: one fixed geography for the whole film. The nun enters from the near end of the cave and stops in the center of the sulfur arena. The dark far end of the cave lies straight ahead of her, and that is where the angel rises. The angel is always in front of her, never behind or beside her. Keep screen direction consistent in every shot: the nun on the left side of the frame facing right, the angel on the right side facing left.

Shot 1 (0-2s): Extreme wide abyssal shot from high in the cave ceiling, the tiny white nun walks into the empty arena far below, god rays falling around her.
Shot 2 (2-4s): Slow tracking at ground level beside her boots, sulfur crust cracking under each step, machete hanging from her hand.
Shot 3 (4-6s): Close-up, her porcelain mask turns slowly, scanning the cave. The ground trembles, dust and spores rain from the ceiling, the acid pools ripple.
Shot 4 (6-8s): Over-the-shoulder from behind the nun looking ahead into the darkness at the far end of the cave: deep in the gloom, two burning points ignite high above, far higher than she expected.
Shot 5 (8-11s): Slow push-in toward the far end: out of the penumbra the colossal fallen angel steps forward, its body emerging from the shadows piece by piece, rusted iron catching the god rays, each step shaking the floor and sending ripples across the acid pools.
Shot 6 (11-14s): Extreme low angle from the floor in front of the angel: its giant wings unfold and ignite one after the other in a massive burst of flame that turns the whole cave orange, the god rays turn red, a storm of embers fills the air. The camera tilts up and up along its body to reveal its full impossible height, the barbed-wire halo flaring red-hot.
Shot 7 (14-16s): Reverse shot from high behind the angel's shoulder looking down at the tiny nun far below, she holds her ground in the center of the arena, embers falling around her.
Shot 8 (16-18s): Extreme close-up of the angel's cracked porcelain face lowering toward her, dry and expressionless, firelight flickering in the cracks.
Shot 9 (18-20s): Wide shot in profile, held: the tiny white nun on the left raises her machete, the colossal burning angel on the right towers over her with its wings spread wall to wall, an empty floor of sulfur between them. End on this held image, no fade, no cut to black.

Real footage look, epic scale, heavy atmosphere, no fighting, no blood, no tears, stable characters, consistent spatial continuity and colossal scale throughout.

PROMPT 2⃣ · THE FIGHT (30s)
Refs: [Image1] nun sheet · [Image2] fallen angel sheet · [Image3] still from clip 1

Brutal dark-fantasy battle filmed like an epic Hollywood blockbuster, real footage look, anamorphic lens, crushed blacks, saturated magenta flesh walls, sulfur yellow and acid green pools, burning orange firelight, god rays, speed ramps from full speed into razor-sharp slow motion, rapid-fire hard cuts every 1 second in the action beats, whip pans, crash zooms, constant motion, no pauses. [Image3] is the reference for the cave, the lighting and the positions of both characters; the video does not open on that exact frame. Nun: [Image1], white habit, cracked porcelain kintsugi mask with no mouth, big rusty machete that she grips firmly in her hand in every single shot, she never drops or releases it. Fallen angel: [Image2], rusted iron body, burning wings, cracked dry porcelain face mask with no tears, barbed-wire halo, colossal, many times taller than the nun.
Spatial continuity: one fixed geography as in [Image3]. The nun starts on the left of the arena facing right, the angel stands on the right facing left, the big dark boulder on the far right, the cave opening behind them. Keep screen direction consistent: the nun moves left to right toward the angel, the angel attacks right to left.

Shot 1 (0-2s): Over-the-shoulder from behind the nun, her white veil and machete in the foreground, the colossal angel in the background at the far end of the arena starts charging its attack, wings igniting; the nun breaks into a sprint toward it, the angel sweeps its burning wing down and a towering tidal wave of roaring fire, twenty meters high, races across the floor toward her, swirling with molten embers and black smoke.
Shot 2 (2-3s): She leaps sideways onto the flesh wall and runs along it horizontally, defying gravity, the wave of fire passing below her.
Shot 3 (3-4s): Whip pan, a second burning wing strike smashes the wall where she was, she kicks off and flips across the cave to the opposite wall, landing crouched on it sideways.
Shot 4 (4-5s): Crash zoom, she springs up and thrusts the machete forward without letting go of it: a blinding spell of white holy light bursts from the tip of the blade in a spear of light.
Shot 5 (5-6s): The colossal angel twists aside at the last instant, the spear of light misses by inches and blasts a glowing crater into the flesh wall behind it.
Shot 6 (6-7s): Close-up of the angel's porcelain mask turning toward her, its halo heating white-hot.
Shot 7 (7-8s): The halo fires a blazing vortex of white-hot fire and molten gold that spirals across the cave; she bounces from wall to wall to ceiling like a ricochet, the fire vortex chasing her and scorching the rock behind her.
Shot 8 (8-9s): The angel stamps its giant iron foot, the floor cracks open, acid pools erupt as columns of green liquid.
Shot 9 (9-10s): She leaps between the rising acid columns and falling slabs, each jump longer and higher than humanly possible, gaining speed.
Shot 10 (10-11s): The angel beats both wings: thousands of burning feathers shoot at her like a meteor shower of fiery blades, each leaving a trail of flame.
Shot 11 (11-12s): She spins the machete in a blur, feathers sliced in half exploding into sparks around her.
Shot 12 (12-13s): She runs straight up the cave wall toward the ceiling, the angel's huge hand crushes the rock just below her heels, she pushes off the ceiling and dives down toward it with full momentum.
Shot 13 (13-15s): Wide, the angel rears back and its whole body ignites: a colossal inferno of fire spirals into its chest and halo like a miniature sun, flames erupting from every crack in its iron, the walls glowing red-hot, while the nun dives at it from above.
Shot 14 (15-20s): Frozen time. The nun leaps and rises into the air as if levitating, body arched in attack position, machete raised over her head toward the angel's face. At the peak of the leap time locks completely. Slow 360 orbit around her suspended in mid-air: embers hang as perfect beads of light, burning feathers float motionless like glowing blades, acid droplets hang as glassy green spheres with perfect surface tension, the angel's charged fire frozen as a still sphere of flame in its chest, the angel's face frozen inches from her blade. Only she moves: her head tilts slightly toward the mask. Time snaps back to full speed.
Shot 15 (20-21s): Slow motion impact, her machete strikes the angel's porcelain mask: the mask shatters into hundreds of porcelain shards that spin through the firelight, the charged attack collapses in a burst of sparks.
Shot 16 (21-22s): Reverse shot, the shards rain down around the nun as she lands on the angel's shoulder.
Shot 17 (22-24s): Wide, the colossal angel staggers, its halo dims, it crashes down onto both knees, the impact shakes the whole cave, rocks fall from the ceiling.
Shot 18 (24-26s): Rapid-fire cuts: she yanks the angel's head back by the barbed-wire halo, slams her boot onto its chest, forcing it down, the angel's broken face looks up at her, embers exploding around them.
Shot 19 (26-30s): Final shot: the nun leaps high one last time, spins in the air and comes down with a savage two-handed overhead swing of the rusty machete straight at the angel's neck, full speed, all her weight behind it, a shockwave of dust and embers bursting outward from the force of the swing. Crash zoom on the blade, hard cut exactly at the instant before the blade touches, the last frame is the blade about to hit. No fade, the blow never lands on screen.

Real footage look, epic scale, heavy atmosphere, no blood, no gore, no tears, the nun always holding her machete, stable characters, consistent spatial continuity and colossal scale throughout.

[ref_5]: the audience.

[AUDIO]

Live TV realism, coherent physics, stable identities, his size constant, natural motion blur.
